system.summary: Second key of Morosini's legation (DECODE 'F22b'): syllables and letters in one- or two-digit figures run together, several homophones for common syllables, no nulls, three-digit nomenclator with a dot on the first digit.

diacritics.note: dot on the first digit marks a nomenclator code

system.sibling_key: Meister 1906 no. 40 (the other 34 Francia 22 enclosures, targets/morosini1588) is a different key
system.notes: Decoded with the morosini1588 beam-search decoder (decrypt.py --f22b), Lasry's values, Italian 5-gram model.

prior_solution.where: Lasry's partial F22b key reconstruction on DECODE R53/R54 (D3187/D3188, 24 Oct 2020); no decryption posted

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code and posed the problem; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE records R18-R58 with the session cookie; R53/R54 carry a second key file (Lasry, 'ASV - F22b').
Wrote decrypt.py: beam search over 1-3 digit segmentations with the Italian 5-gram model, nomenclator for dotted codes.
Applied Lasry's partial F22b reconstruction (~70 elements) to R53/R54.
Partial-reading audit: R53/R54 listed as the open gap of the Francia 22 entry (second key, no further key material).
Meister 1906 (OCR) searched for a second Morosini key: index lists him only at p. 393 (no. 40); no. 32 (Bishop of Brescia with Rinalducci, 1585-90) is a cover-name list, not this syllabary.
rebuild.py: values for the 24 empty two-figure codes by coordinate ascent on the decoder's LM score, Lasry's values fixed, fitted on R53 and on R54 separately.
Held-out check of the two fits: they agree on 1 code of about 10 (84 c) and each breaks readable stretches of the other record; no value adopted, reading kept on Lasry's key.
measure_sense.py: 0.752 of decoded letters in attested Italian words (R53 0.791, R54 0.707) against 0.817 for the 34 fully read Meister-key records.
Split from morosini1588 under the one-key rule: R53/R54 (F22b key) made their own entry; transcriptions, Lasry's key files and the decoder output moved here; Lasry credit scoped to the F22b key.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE cipher transcriptions D1717/D1825; decryptions = the word-split decoder output copied from decode_updates/decryptions into texts/, plus plaintext_by_record.txt (both with Lasry's F22b key, decode/DOC_R53_D3187_3187.txt / DOC_R54_D3188_3188.txt).

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R53_decryption.txt, R54_decryption.txt and plaintext_by_record.txt read: R53 has Italian fragments with garbled strings in nearly every sentence, R54 is mostly noise (docs/_check_reading.py: 6 of 15 and 5 of 12 sentences clean in the word-split files). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.752 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b21). Every file on DECODE R53 and R54 fetched with the shared cookie (b17_fetch.py) into the session scratchpad: the two page images, the transcriptions and Lasry's key file (already in decode/), and five png attachments never opened before. R53: DOC_R53_D1080 = f. 499r, the clear letter ('Giunsi à Molins ...', Morosini's illness), D1094 = f. 498v, address and docket ('1589, 4 di maggio ... da Molins'). R54: D1081 = f. 502v, address and docket; D1099 = f. 500r and D1095 = f. 500v, a complete contemporary decipherment of both cipher passages, R53 on 500r ('Il Navarro per quello che mi disse domenica ...' to '... di Umena, al quale si tiene') and R54 on 500v ('se gli andavano ingrossando ogni giorno ...' to '... essendo distrutti i primi fondamenti').

Both pages of the decipherment transcribed from native-resolution strips: texts/R53_decifrato_f500r.txt (15 lines), R54_decifrato_f500v.txt (14 lines), abbreviations expanded in brackets, the decipherer's struck words, superscript code (1̇85 over 'Navarro') and marginal '1 non' recorded.

b21_moro_align.py: dynamic programming over figures and decipherment letters (elements of 1-2 figures, 3 for nomenclator codes; Lasry's key; unkeyed elements may stand for 1-4 letters; doubled consonants of the decipherer as extra letters). First run (Lasry's key only): 4 is unkeyed and stands for 'c' at every one of its 17 places (in che, chi: 4 98, 4 9 5); undotted 185 is the Navarro code 1̇85 (dot not marked in D1717, three places); 216 = me, 130 = ma as Lasry has them.

Value adopted: 4 = c (17 places in R53/R54, all 'c' in the decipherment; texts/f22b_values_b21.tsv). With it Lasry's 495/498 = chi read c-h-e, the decipherer's 'che' at every place; no 'chi' occurs in the decipherment. Not adopted (one occurrence each, value only from the decipherment): 57 q, 117, 637, 42 (fra/ge, inconsistent), 53 0, 81, 38, 27 lu, 75, 11. 89 (Lasry si) stands for 'se' in fosero, disegnaua and for 'si' in 'si tiene': kept as si/se.

Disagreements between figures and decipherment checked word by word (texts/R53_words.tsv, R54_words.tsv; 101 of 155 and 85 of 131 words given letter for letter by the key, the rest mostly the cipher's single consonants). Figures followed where they give another word: R53 grosa (decipherer 'grandi'), la fece ('lo'), la quale ('Le quali'), ne ('vi'), Lemans ('Limans'), erano ('sono', R53 last line on the image: 1̇16 5 41 36 130 = re e-ra-no ma); R54 lo habbia, dagli, tutto quello. R53 l. 10 checked on the image: 'dabene' is written 76 28 70 (da-gi-ne), an encipherer's slip; the reading keeps the decipherer's word.

Readings written on the decipherment with the figures' words where they differ (texts/R53_reading.md, R54_reading.md; English R53_en.md, R54_en.md). R53's last clause runs on into R54 ('al quale si tiene se gli andavano ingrossando ogni giorno'). _check_reading.py on the bodies: R53 0.833 (10/12), R54 1.0 (11/11); before (decode files) 0.40 and 0.42. Both set read, grade A; class not read -> read, method -> read from existing decipherment, fraction_read 0 -> 1.0.

outcome.method_basis: R53 and R54 read on 23 Oct 2026 from their 1589 decipherment (ff. 500r-500v, png attachments on DECODE R54 that had not been opened), aligned element by element with the figures under George Lasry's partial F22b reconstruction (2020) and one value adopted from the alignment (4 = c); the figures are followed where they give another word.

gaps.item: R53, R54: single elements whose value only the decipherment gives (57 q, 117, 637, 42, 53/0, 81, 38, 27 lu, 75, 11; 29 elements in all, listed in texts/f22b_values_b21.tsv)
gaps.detail: one occurrence each in 1,448 figures: not adopted as key values; the reading rests on the decipherment there

gaps.item: R53, R54: words where the figures give no Italian word (mi disse domenica, francesi, seco, dabene, dissegni, al quale si tiene; di qui, fin hora, perche, distrutti i primi)
gaps.detail: lone figures or doubtful digits in DECODE's transcription (R54's has about 40 '?' marks); not re-transcribed from the image here except R53 l. 10 ('76 28 70' for 'dabene', a slip of the encipherer)

outcome.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from morosini1588 (one key per entry). Measured 14 Oct 2026 (sense measure, see fraction_read_source). Key-rebuild by coordinate ascent on the 24 empty two-figure codes: fits on R53 and on R54 agree on one code of about ten and break each other's readable stretches; not adopted. 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b21): both enclosures read from their 1589 decipherment on ff. 500r-500v (png attachments of DECODE R54, never opened before), aligned with the figures; one key value adopted (4 = c, 17 places); class not read -> read.

texts.label: R53, Francia 22/32, image 499v, [Moulins, early May 1589; decipherment f. 500r]
texts.summary: Navarre, by what the vice-legate of Avignon's secretary said, arrived at Tours on Thursday and lodged at Plessis with a large company; he went to see the King, gave him the shirt at his rising and the napkin at table, and dined with him: a mixing of heretics and Catholics at court, hateful to honest men. Navarre was to review his troops before the King and, joined by Turenne's men, push against Mayenne, between Le Mans and Vendôme; the King's forces were greater than Mayenne's. The 1589 decipherment on f. 500r (DECODE attachment DOC_R54_D1099) and the figures read together.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b21): the 1589 decipherment on f. 500r (DECODE R54 attachment DOC_R54_D1099, '500r.jpg [cleartext]', never opened before) transcribed and aligned element by element with the figures under Lasry's F22b key plus 4 = c, adopted at all 17 places in R53/R54 (b21_moro_align.py, texts/R53_align.tsv, R53_words.tsv, f22b_values_b21.tsv). 603 of 693 letters are the figures' own value; the rest are the decipherer's doubled consonants and words where the figures slip or a code has no value; no letter rests on a look-alike alternate. Figures followed against the decipherer in six words (grosa, la fece, la quale, ne, Lemans, erano). _check_reading.py on the body 0.833 (10/12); the decode file 0.40.

texts.label: R54, Francia 22/33, image 502r, Moulins, 11 May 1589
texts.summary: Continues R53 (Mayenne's forces growing daily). With Navarre at the King's side and heretics mixed with Catholics at court, the Pope will be the more resolved to recall Morosini; if not, any lords wanting him back at court must understand it is impossible unless they send an army to escort and defend him from the heretics; the union cuts the head off all that was discussed at Montalto's departure. The 1589 decipherment on f. 500v (DECODE attachment DOC_R54_D1095) and the figures read together.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b21): the 1589 decipherment on f. 500v (DECODE R54 attachment DOC_R54_D1095, never opened before; it continues the R53 decipherment on f. 500r) transcribed and aligned element by element with the figures under Lasry's F22b key plus 4 = c (texts/R54_align.tsv, R54_words.tsv). 468 of 622 letters are the figures' own value and 61 stand on digits DECODE's transcription marks illegible ('?'), fixed by the decipherment; no letter rests on a look-alike alternate. Figures followed against the decipherer in three words (lo habbia, dagli, tutto quello); 'non' in 'disgratia non fosse' is the decipherer's marginal insertion (no figures). _check_reading.py on the body 1.0 (11/11); the decode file 0.42.
